Illustrative sample

Frontend Delivery Diagnostic

This is a demonstration, not a client case study. The scenario and findings below are illustrative and show how a Nabura Labs diagnostic can organize evidence and decisions.

Scenario

A B2B product team supports five React applications.

The team ships regularly, but shared experiences have diverged, testing is inconsistent, and platform upgrades compete with feature work. Leadership needs a modernization sequence that improves delivery without pausing the roadmap.

Priority finding 01

Shared UI behavior is duplicated across applications.

Evidence
Similar components use different APIs, accessibility behavior, and release processes.
Business impact
Simple experience changes require repeated implementation and coordination.
Recommendation
Define one shared contract and validate it with a high-change component before expanding.
First measure
Compare implementation and review time for the pilot component across two applications.

Priority finding 02

Release confidence depends on manual knowledge.

Evidence
Critical journeys have uneven automated coverage and release checks vary by application.
Business impact
Senior engineers become release bottlenecks and risky changes wait longer.
Recommendation
Establish a small set of shared release gates around the highest-value customer journeys.
First measure
Track rollback, hotfix, and manual verification effort for four releases.

90-day direction

Sequence the work so each step proves the next.

  1. Weeks 1–3: Baseline delivery measures and choose one shared component pilot.
  2. Weeks 4–7: Build the component contract, release path, and adoption guide.
  3. Weeks 8–10: Adopt in two applications and document migration friction.
  4. Weeks 11–13: Decide whether to expand, adjust, or stop based on evidence.
